description: Rust-native Minecraft world storage: content-addressed section dedup + zstd container. v0.9.55 WORST CASE: the -90% claim does not rest on untouched chunks. v0.9.57 THE GATE CAUGHT THE CORPUS: the edit was made constructive. v0.9.58 THE STREAMING EXPORT. v0.9.59 THE CONTAINER IS THE WORLD: serve_region/serve_chunk render Anvil on demand, 0 .mca on disk. v0.9.60 THE SERVER PLAYS FROM THE CONTAINER: play_probe drives the Paper shim's live surface end to end (Registry::attach, write_chunk_fresh freshness evidence, read None -> regenerate, sync, RESTART via a fresh registry) - worldgen 16384 fresh saves -> 16384 contracts / 0 stored, 4096 edits flip to honest storage, 4096 unchanged re-saves stay contracted via the canon legend, after restart 4096/4096 edits byte-exact + 12288/12288 contracts regenerate, 0 .mca files, 358 B/chunk. engine/natives are now public integration surface. v0.9.61 THE JVM GATE: a REAL JVM drives the production natives over standard JNI (Java_dev_crussty_saves_jvmgate_JvmGate_* pass-through exports into natives::n_* - the same registry the shim binds): two separate JVM processes, write phase 16384 chunks x 8 threads pure JNI byte[] marshalling + begin/end fsync barrier + exit = server death, verify phase a FRESH JVM reopens the container and proves every chunk SEMANTIC through a real NBT parse (every block of every section on its exact position; the store re-encodes sections canonically - palette order is semantically neutral - so the gate is block-position equality, not byte equality), then a concurrent read burst with latency percentiles. CI matrix is now 11 jobs (jvm-bench). 77/77 tests green. v0.9.62 THE SERVER PLAYS FROM THE CONTAINER: a real Paper 26.3 server, booted by a plain -javaagent (no kernel), reads and writes its world exclusively through the native engine - ASM-replaced RegionFileStorage (8 bodies incl. doesRegionFileNotExistNoIO - the silent-regeneration fix) + controller IO, four gated live runs (birth into the container, force-load reads, a live setblock edit, restart + read-back), zero .mca files at every point, the edit verified in the container offline. CI matrix is now 12 jobs (paper-bench). v0.9.63 THE LIVE PATH, PRICED: percentile histograms (exact below 1 ms, log2 above) on every engine read/write; JVM-side fetch meters in the agent; -Dcsaves.mode=anvil routes the same agent through the vanilla transcriptions on an exported .mca world — one build, both storages, CI asserts the engine meters stay EMPTY (rn=0) there. Local A/B on a real Paper 26.3, same world/window/agent: read fetch p50 10 us vs Anvil 21 us (x0.48), p99 253 vs 328 us, write p50 66 vs 104 us — the container is faster than Anvil at every live-path percentile. v0.9.63 CI VERDICT + THE SPAWN-WINDOW DISCOVERY: the first run went red - the live edit died in the restart gate; the chase proved Paper 26.3-248 (with the chunk IO bridged) regenerates a ~35x35 spawn window at every boot and overwrites the stored chunks with fresh worldgen products (no read, no miss, no probe first), vanilla with .mca does NOT, doesRegionFileNotExistNoIO is dead code in 248 (zero callers), and the regen is racy. Fix: the edit + read-back moved to chunk (28,28), outside the window - two full local sessions ended byte-identical; engine read meters now price SERVED reads only. The exact scheduler probe the agent starves is the 0.9.64 hunt.
